headline: IAF Chief Announces New Air Power Roadmap Featuring Steam-Powered Paper Planes for Stealth Surveillance
body:
Q: The recent roadmap mentioned next-generation platforms like the AMCA, but you’ve focused heavily on a new 'Folded-Stealth' initiative. What is the tactical advantage?

A: It’s about thermal signature management. A traditional jet engine runs hot, but a high-quality A4 sheet of paper folded into a dart shape emits zero infrared signals. Our pilots have spent the last six months perfecting the 'long-distance glide' launch technique from the cockpit to ensure total radar invisibility.

Q: Critics are asking how a paper airplane can effectively carry surveillance equipment or heavy weaponry. Isn't there a payload issue?

A: That is exactly the kind of dated, heavy-metal thinking we are trying to move past. We aren't carrying bombs; we are dropping highly detailed charcoal sketches of enemy positions. It’s low-tech, impossible to hack, and frankly, very aesthetic. If an adversary tries to jam our signal, they’ll just find themselves holding a very nice piece of origami.

Q: Is it true that the entire fleet’s maintenance budget has been diverted to a subscription service for professional-grade stationery?

A: Efficiency is key. Why maintain a multi-billion dollar fleet of complex avionics when you can simply walk into a local bookstore and purchase a pack of recycled cardstock? The logistics are simplified, the carbon footprint is effectively zero, and during the monsoon, we just switch to waterproof wax-coated models.
caption: The IAF’s new strategy is clearly ahead of the curve. Who needs drones when you have a sharp crease and a strong gust of wind? #IAF #AirPower #Aerospace #Innovation (satire)
